title: Ethiopian Beef with Potatoes Wat
localName: ሥጋ ከድንች ወጥ — Siga ke-Dinich Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the budget-friendly everyday wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Beef and Potato Wat — beef cooked in a Key Wat-style berbere sauce with potato chunks added in the final 20 minutes. The budget-extending daily wat — the potatoes absorb the berbere sauce completely and become deeply flavourful.
longDesc: Siga ke-Dinich Wat is the practical everyday version of Key Wat — the addition of potatoes extends a smaller quantity of beef into a full family meal while the potatoes absorb the berbere sauce and become magnificent in their own right.
steps: Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger. Add beef. Coat in sauce.
Potatoes should be completely tender and orange from the berbere.
chefTips: Add potatoes last — they cook faster than beef.
The berbere potatoes are often the most popular element of this dish.
cookingScience: Potato starch absorbs the berbere-infused cooking liquid — drawing the carotenoids from the berbere into the potato flesh, producing the characteristic orange-stained potato that is deeply flavoured throughout.
sustainabilityTips: Extending meat with potatoes — more affordable and nutritious.
healthBenefits: Potatoes add potassium and vitamin C.
culturalNote: Siga ke-Dinich Wat is the honest everyday cooking of Ethiopian families — making the most of what is available, ensuring every ingredient is used to maximum effect.
